root_offenders.verdict: LOCAL PYTHON SCRIPT running a monitoring/polling loop against services on 192.168.2.151 (Mac Mini) and 192.168.1.46

drip_explanation.what: A Python 3.13 process on 192.168.2.46 (your Parrot box) is running an automated polling loop.
mechanism: GET /status on port 7734 every ~7.2 seconds (health check)
GET /api/notes on port 8082 every ~18 seconds (data pull, returns 'crd-mac-mini-bombshell-2026-03-22')
Connections to 192.168.1.46:8083 (cross-subnet, 104 packets with rotating source ports)
drip_explanation.target_device: 192.168.2.151 — likely a Mac Mini (based on 'crd-mac-mini-bombshell' identifier) running custom HTTP services
drip_explanation.why_port_hopping: Ephemeral source ports rotate per-connection (stateless HTTP/1.1 without keepalive). Not actual port hopping evasion — just normal TCP behavior with short-lived connections.
drip_explanation.the_drip: The 'drip' IS the polling loop. Your Python script constantly pings the Mac Mini for status and notes. This generates steady low-bandwidth outbound traffic (the drip pattern).
drip_explanation.is_malicious: NO — this is your own monitoring script talking to your own local infrastructure. The 'crd-mac-mini-bombshell' is a note/identifier on that Mac Mini's API.
drip_explanation.external_traffic: 143.198.246.99 = apackets.com (packet analysis tool website visited via browser). Normal HTTPS. Plus standard browser traffic to Google, DuckDuckGo, Microsoft, Cursor IDE (api2.cursor.sh).

port_map.8082: Custom API server on Mac Mini (serves /api/notes)

reverse_socratic_trace.a: Steady ~7s interval HTTP GETs from 192.168.2.46 to LAN devices
Dst ports 7734, 8082, 8083. Source ports are ephemeral (normal TCP).
You wrote a monitoring/polling script that checks your Mac Mini's services in a loop. This IS the drip.
Same pattern (port 8083), likely another device you're monitoring. Different subnet suggests VPN, VLAN, or dual-homed network.

council_summary.red_council: Flagged port-hopping pattern (8 non-standard ports) and regular beaconing. Scored MEDIUM.
council_summary.blue_council: 72% HTTPS dominant, infrastructure DNS normal, bandwidth extremely low. Scored INFO.
council_summary.final_maker: BLUE PREVAILS. The 'port hopping' is actually normal ephemeral source port rotation on short-lived HTTP connections. The beaconing IS real but it's YOUR OWN script polling YOUR OWN devices. Not malicious.

recommendations: To identify the exact script: run `sudo lsof -i :7734` and `sudo lsof -i :8082` on 192.168.2.46 while it's active
Or: `ps aux | grep python` to find the Python 3.13 process
The script likely lives in a cron or systemd service — check `crontab -l` and `systemctl list-units`
To reduce drip: increase polling intervals or switch to event-driven (websocket/SSE)
